newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Palladium, platinum volatile at fresh high.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Palladium, platinum volatile at fresh high.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Palladium and platinum could surge further after hitting fresh highs overnight on news of an illegal strike at Anglo American's Rustenburg operation, dealers and analysts said.
But the market was very volatile and could seen huge swings either way, they warned.
Gold and silver were steady and consolidating but could probe lower if the PGMs see a correction.
PALLADIUM -
The market was volatile after prices surged to a fresh high of $188 per ounce overnight on news that 4,600 South African miners at Anglo American went on an illegal strike.
Prices were likely to surge again, especially if a large American hedge fund added to positions, a senior dealer said.
But prices were vulnerable to a sharp correction on further news of deliveries from Russia or if the hedge fund began to take profits, he added.
"I could see the price going higher or dropping $10 to $15 in a matter of minutes," he said.
Another dealer said he though the reaction to the South African strike was exaggerated, but in a tight market sentiment was powerful.
Even though one-month lease rates were still at 41 percent, some players preferred to borrow since they regarded the price as overextended, he added.
It was difficult to use charts since prices had surpassed the highs achieved in 1989 and there was little historical data, the dealer said.
At 0745 GMT spot palladium was quoted at $186/$188 per ounce, compared to Tuesday's New York close of $175.50/$176.50.
PLATINUM -
The market also had scope for higher prices above $400, but it too was vulnerable to a correction.
The price of $406 per ounce equalled the peak seen in February this year, when prices were the highest since May 1996.
Above $406, resistance was pegged around $410, the highs seen in late March and April 1996, then around $415/6, analysts said.
At 0745 GMT, spot platinum was quoted at $404.00/$405.50 compared to Tuesday's New York close of 398.00/$399.00.
GOLD -
The market was seen consolidating, underpinned by higher levels in the PGM complex.
"Underlying support continues to hold...as the technical indicators creep higher," said analyst Martin Squires at broker Rudolf.
With the successive higher lows over the past week, there is more chance of an upward break through resistance at $345 and $346, he added, referring to the Comex June contract.
Analyst John Sowden of Elliott Wave International said limited gains could be seen towards $344.75, basis spot gold, as long as nearby support at $343.30 holds.
But a drop through that floor would be the first hint that the larger downtrend was back on track to below $339.95, he added.
At 0800 GMT spot gold was quoted at $344.60/345.00, up from Tuesday's New York close of $343.80/$344.30.
SILVER -
Further sideways activity is expected with an upward bias, analysts said.
Resistance was pegged at $4.80 and support at $4.70, analysts said.
At 0800 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.76/4.78, up from Tuesday's New York close of $4.75/$4.77. --Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
